turnaround_reason: Down from $73.74 to ~$43 on falling US residential solar demand, tariff margin drag, and a post-tax-credit-expiration pull-forward hangover, but Q1 2026 revenue and battery shipments beat and management is guiding sequential improvement into Q2/Q3 helped by Europe recovery and commercial solar growth.
bullish_points: Q1 2026 beat: $282.9M revenue, $83M FCF, non-GAAP gross margin ~44%
Insider buying from CEO Kothandaraman ($337K purchase in May) and a director purchase in June — real skin in the game, not just grants
Early signs of European demand recovery and growing US commercial solar mix offsetting weak residential
Tariff drag easing sequentially (4.3pp hit in Q1 vs 5.1pp in Q4) — margin headwind is decelerating
Cheap on forward earnings (17.9x forward P/E vs 42.6x trailing) if the guide holds
bearish_points: Revenue still down -20.6% YoY on a TTM basis — this is a company still shrinking, not yet growing
Operating margin is negative (-9.1%) despite positive net margin, meaning the core business isn't yet profitable on an operating basis
US residential solar demand remains structurally challenged post-tax-credit changes — the main growth engine is impaired
Q2 guide of $280-310M implies flat-to-down sequential revenue including $85M of one-time safe-harbor revenue, which masks underlying weakness
High debt-to-equity (55.5x) for a company with negative operating margins is a real risk if the recovery stalls
suggested_trade: Spot position ahead of July 28 earnings, or a Jan 2027 $45/$55 call spread for defined-risk leverage on a beat-and-guide-up
key_risk: US residential solar demand fails to stabilize and Q2 print shows the safe-harbor revenue was masking a deeper shrinkage in core business — stock likely revisits 52-week lows near $26
would_skip_if: Q2 guide is missed or safe-harbor revenue continues to be the only source of sequential growth with core residential still declining double digits
